PullRequest.Title: refactor(sessions): move sessions list grouping and sorting helpers to sessionsListHelpers.ts
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Why
Move 2 of phase 2 of splitting the 11.5k-line `sessionsList.ts` into smaller modules. It is stacked on #349657 and moves the pure list helpers, so they can be used and tested without loading the list control.

## What changed
- New `sessionsListHelpers.ts` with these declarations, byte for byte: the Approval Helpers, Folder Matching, and Sorting & Grouping Helpers regions (`groupSessionsForList`, `groupBy*`, `sortSessions`, `limitSessionsForList`, `computeReorderSortChanges`, …), plus the section ID constants and five small helpers they use (`getChatTitle`, `getSessionListChats`, `isShortcutSection`, `isSessionGroupingSection`, `getSessionSectionType`).
- The only edits: `export` added to 34 declarations that `sessionsList.ts` still uses, import lines updated in 5 files (tests included), and the moved blocks deleted. Nothing is re-exported from `sessionsList.ts`.

## Scope
No behavior changes.

## Blast Radius
Module load order only: the moved code has no module-level side effects, the new module does not import `sessionsList.ts`, and there is no import cycle. The 39 moved `localize` calls now belong to `sessionsListHelpers`, so language packs pick them up from the next translation pass.

## Verification
- Move check (a TypeScript compiler API script): all 257 top-level declaration blocks are identical before and after, ignoring the 34 added `export` keywords; the other 5 files changed only their imports.
- `typecheck-client`, `valid-layers-check`, `check-cyclic-dependencies`, and `oxlint` on the 6 changed files pass.
- Sessions list unit tests and their importers: 6,992 tests, the same as base.
- Component fixtures (`sessionsList`, `sessionsListNotification`, `sessionsInboxScope`, `blockedSessionsList`): all 346 screenshots match base.
- Bundled CSS (desktop, web, server-web, mobile): all 6 files are byte-identical.
- In Code OSS (Agents window, base and head): all grouping modes, Find, the context menu, drag and drop, and the blocked-sessions list give the same rows, the screenshots match, and the console shows no new errors.

Details are in the first comment.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold startup and loading session actions or the blocked-sessions indicator
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The importing modules must evaluate before their consumers run. The extracted module initializes small section constants and declares helpers; it does not instantiate list controls, approval models, or services.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/browser/views/sessionsListHelpers.ts:7-22 and updated imports in sessionsList.ts, sessionsListActions.ts, sessionsViewActions.ts, blockedSessionsIndicatorModel.ts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load and evaluate the extracted ES module and its existing dependencies.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One evaluation per module identity per runtime, shared by all importers; not one evaluation per session or helper invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Helpers were evaluated within sessionsList.ts. Their runtime dependencies were already imported by that module; the changed importers previously referenced the list module.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold module loading precedes consumer execution. Warm imports reuse the evaluated module.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct loaded modules, not session or chat count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Module evaluation follows dependency ordering; the extraction does not launch asynchronous work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Normal ES-module caching shares helpers and dependencies across importers. No new application cache, negative-cache behavior, or per-consumer singleton is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all added module-level declarations and updated import hunks were inspected; no heavyweight initialization or new repeated dependency evaluation was found.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Bundled startup timing and byte-delivery costs were not measured. A single additional module is not evidence of an actionable regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Import targets change, but the moved code does not introduce eager product work. There is insufficient evidence of a concrete historical performance regression being fixed to submit a regression-fix signal.

Scenarios.Scenario: Display, filter, regroup, sort, expand, or refresh the sessions tree
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SessionsList.update synchronously filters existing session state, sorts members, groups sections, applies visibility limits, and supplies rows to the existing tree. These computations precede the refreshed rows.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: N included sessions, G resulting sections, chats within each session, and comparison participants. Session sorting remains O(N log N); bucket allocation and date partitioning retain their existing collection scaling. Existing worktree comparator scans remain unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI-thread computation. scheduleListUpdate still coalesces pending updates into one animation-frame callback and defers hidden-list work; the extraction does not alter scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Per-call grouping maps and arrays remain temporary. The existing session state, sort-key service, inbox-placement equality suppression, and hidden-view deferral are unchanged. Repository and worktree helpers read existing metadata and parse URIs; they do not query GitHub or the filesystem.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: deleted helper bodies were compared with additions, and update, refreshSessions, animation-frame scheduling, repository metadata access, and path-only worktree recognition were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large-list sizes and render duration were not measured, but no algorithm, invocation frequency, or visibility cap changes in this diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Existing sorting, allocations, grouping scans, comparison processing, and list limits are relocated without increasing their cost or frequency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Show pending approvals in session rows and classify blocked-session attention
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Visible row computations and blocked-session classification read the approval model. Main-tree rows inspect the main chat; flat lists and blocked-session classifications scan chats to select the oldest approval.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One main-chat lookup per nonaggregating row; aggregate calls scan C chats per applicable session. Multiple existing classification consumers retain their prior call counts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous observable reads, with the same model shared by the indicator and dropdown. No requests are issued by getApproval.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: AgentSessionApprovalModel.getApproval reuses resource-keyed weakly held observables and creates an undefined observable on a miss. Finalization and model-tracker disposal remain unchanged; the extracted helpers do not create their own model or cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both aggregate and main-chat implementations match the deleted bodies, their row and indicator consumers are unchanged, and the approval model's weak cache and lifecycle were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Chat count and observable invalidation frequency vary; neither multiplicity nor ownership changes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. No new scans, remote reads, observable retention, or model instances are introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Choose a source for a new session from a repository, workspace, or environment section
Scenarios.CriticalPath: getNewSessionSources examines existing sessions, checks creation-target availability, and selects the newest reusable session per environment. The action then opens the composer and selects its workspace or environment. openNewSessionLike calls openNewSession without a folder, so this call takes the existing composer path rather than concrete-session creation or its workspace-trust gate.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: S sessions in the selected section, P registered providers consulted by availability checks for applicable cloud repository roots, and E distinct connected environments after grouping. Results contain at most one source per environment.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Source selection and availability checks remain synchronous. The action retains its single await for opening the composer; no per-source asynchronous creation fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The source map is temporary. Provider routing, connection status, workspace metadata, and cloud task metadata are read from existing state. No positive, negative, or in-flight cache is added or defeated.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: moved source-selection functions were compared against the deleted bodies; inheritableSessionTarget, provider lookup, availability checks, cloud creation-target implementations, action consumers, and the folderless composer branch were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider count and section size vary, and downstream workspace-picker duration was not measured. The selected source and downstream calls are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Environment grouping and service-call frequency are identical; the diff changes only where the helpers are imported.

Scenarios.Scenario: Drag sessions to reorder them and persist manual sort overrides
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing drop handlers determine neighbors and natural keys, call computeReorderSortChanges, and apply the resulting changes. The helper still performs linear work in the dragged block before returning.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Convert the created/updated override maps to objects and JSON-encode them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once when an applySortChanges call actually changes overrides, not once per dragged item; serialized size scales with retained overrides across the two modes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same helper output fed the same applySortChanges and saveSortOverrides code with identical serialization frequency and payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous encoding occurs while applying changes before the change event.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update or remove the profile-storage key for sort overrides through IStorageService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One storage-key operation per changed override batch. An additional existing default-placement save may occur when that separate state changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same storage calls occurred for the same changes before extraction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The storage-service call is made during applying the drop; the code does not await durable persistence.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: D dragged sessions, sessions considered while locating neighbors, and K retained sort overrides serialized per changed batch.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Drop computation and map application remain synchronous; persistence is performed once after batching mutations, with no new tasks or concurrent writes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Persistent override maps remain owned by SessionsListModelService and are loaded once from profile storage. The helper's result Map and clear array are temporary, and natural-fit clearing behavior is preserved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: computeReorderSortChanges is unchanged apart from location, and drop consumers, applySortChanges, and persistence were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Override-history size and backend flush latency were not measured; neither serialization size nor call count increases.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Computation, clearing semantics, retained state, and batched serialization remain unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Mark eligible nested chats as read across selected sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action filters chats with getSessionListChats, excludes already-read chats, and calls markChatsRead. That service prefers the provider's bulk API; the agent-host implementation updates cached state and dispatches actions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch ChatIsReadChanged actions through the local or remote agent-host connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For a supported connected agent host, one dispatch per eligible unread nested chat despite one bulk service call per selected session. Missing cached sessions/connections or empty chat collections issue no dispatch. Legacy protocol/provider fallback uses the existing single-chat path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same chat filter, bulk preference, per-chat dispatch loop, and fallback existed before the helper import changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Dispatch is issued within markChatsRead; the action starts work with Promise.all and returns without awaiting it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Selected nonarchived sessions supporting independent chat read state and their eligible unread peer chats after excluding main, tool, hidden, archived, and conditionally side chats.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The action invokes per-session service calls through Promise.all. Modern agent-host bulk calls mutate state in a transaction and synchronously issue their per-chat dispatches; fallback single-chat calls retain their prior Promise.all behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing cached sessions, chats, read state, and connection initialization are reused. Already-read chats are filtered before the provider call; no new miss retries or remote reads are introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the relocated filter matches the deleted implementation, and the action, service bulk/fallback handling, and agent-host dispatch loop were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Selection size, chat count, protocol version, and transport latency vary; effective fan-out and concurrency are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR neither increases eligible chat cardinality nor changes batching, dispatch count, concurrency, or cache ownership.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the distinct performance-review pass across all six changed files and every diff page. The helper extraction preserves function bodies and consumers, with only exports, constants' locations, and import targets changing. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or proven historical regression fix was found. Conclusions are based on static code and call-path analysis, not runtime timing or profiling.
